title: Claude Code mods, from zero: a cleaner chat and how to build one
summary: Anthropic shipped Claude Code mods on 1 October 2026. This guide explains them from zero: what a mod is, why it matters, what people built in the first…
body_markdown:
**Builder guide**


**No experience needed**


**Terminal and desktop**


**Open source, MIT**


October 2026


[chat-clean achammah/claude-chat-clean · MIT · Terminal and desktop View on GitHub](https://github.com/achammah/claude-chat-clean)


The short version


- **Claude Code mods are new.** Anthropic shipped them on 1 October 2026, in Claude Code 2.1.287.
- **A mod is a small add-on that changes how Claude Code looks and behaves.** You can write one, or ask Claude to build it for you.
- **The big idea: you shape the tool to how you work.** See what the agent is doing, use the waiting time, keep secrets out of the chat. No waiting for a new feature.
- **People built mods within hours.** Progress bars, usage meters, games, a way to keep passwords out of the chat.
- **We built one to clean up the chat.** chat-clean keeps your words and Claude's replies, and folds the work into one line per turn.
- **The cost is trust.** Mods are not sandboxed. Install them only from sources you trust.
- **Try ours in three steps.** chat-clean is free and open source at[github.com/achammah/claude-chat-clean](https://github.com/achammah/claude-chat-clean) .


## 1


Claude Code mods, the new update


Claude Code is Anthropic's coding assistant. It works on the files of a project: it reads them, changes them and runs commands. On , Anthropic made it possible to change Claude Code itself, with mods.


- **When.** Mods arrived in . The release note reads: "Added Claude Mods: plugins may now modify deeper behavior" ([changelog](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) ).
- **Where.** In the terminal from version 2.1.287, and in the desktop app from ([docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/overview) ). They are on by default.

Mods ship inside plugins, so you install them with /plugin in the CLI or desktop app. A few examples: View the post on X](https://x.com/ClaudeDevs/status/2105721434807083061)

Each person works differently, so there's no reason why everyone should have an identical Claude experience. Make Claude your own, and share mods as plugins so others can try your mods too. Each person works differently, so there's no reason why everyone should have an identical Claude experience."


### What a mod is


- **In one sentence.** A mod is a small add-on that runs when something happens in Claude Code, such as a tool call, a message you send, or a part of the screen being drawn. It can watch that moment, change it, or take it over ([docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/overview) ).
- **How you get one.** Mods ship inside plugins, so you install them with` /plugin` , like any other plugin.
- **Who can make one.** Anyone. Anthropic's[announcement](https://claude.com/blog/claude-code-mods) : "Ask Claude to create a mod, and it can write the TypeScript, install it, and hot reload it in your session."


### The five things a mod can do


The[docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/overview) list five. In plain words:


1. **Add its own panel.** A pane beside the chat, or a band just above where you type, with tabs, buttons and text fields.
2. **Redraw Claude Code's own screen.** For example a tool call's row, the spinner, or the box where Claude asks you a question.
3. **Step into an action.** Hold a tool call while it asks you something, answer it without running the tool, or send a request to a different model.
4. **Run your own command at once.** A slash command that runs your code right away, even while Claude is working.
5. **Share what it learns.** What one part of a mod records, another part can show.


Anthropic is moving its own features to mods too: "the built-in /diff feature is now a mod, so you can turn it off (in /plugin) or replace it with your own version" ([announcement](https://claude.com/blog/claude-code-mods) ).


**So what?** Until now you could only change what you ask Claude Code. With a mod, you can change Claude Code itself.


## 2


Why mods matter


Claude Code already had hooks: small scripts that run at set moments. Anthropic explains the step up: "Hooks helped give users some of this control, but hooks can't rewrite events, draw new UI, or replace features. Mods can." ([announcement](https://claude.com/blog/claude-code-mods) )


### What you gain


- **You shape the tool to how you work.** You no longer wait for a feature. In Anthropic's words: "We want Claude Code to feel like yours, so you can shape it to the way you work."
- **You see what the agent does, live.** Most early mods show something at a glance: the progress of a plan, what a session is working on, the state of your code, or how much usage is left (section 3).
- **The waiting time becomes useful.** One mod puts games above the prompt, "playable while Claude works, zero tokens" ([cc-arcade](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/91870#issuecomment-5666255143) ). Another user[wrote](https://x.com/halluton/status/2099640486130835845) : "I made one that makes you breathe while Claude thinks". Boris Cherny[answered](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2099640866969448834) : "Yes!!!"
- **You do not need to code.** Ask Claude to write it. One developer[put it simply](https://dev.to/pawel_nowak/i-built-my-first-claude-code-mod-without-writing-code-claude-wrote-it-validated-it-and-2mh7) : "I described a UI in plain English, and it showed up."
- **It goes deeper than hooks.** A mod can change a moment before it happens. One mod keeps passwords out of the chat history (section 3).
- **You can share it.** Mods ship as plugins, so others can install yours. A[community catalogue](https://github.com/karanb192/awesome-claude-code-mods) already lists them.


### The cost: trust


- **A mod can do what Claude Code can do.** Anthropic is clear: "They aren't sandboxed, and you should only install mods from sources you trust" ([announcement](https://claude.com/blog/claude-code-mods) ).
- **Check before you install.**` claude plugin validate <folder>` lists the events a mod handles and what it asks Claude Code to do ([docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/overview) ).


**So what?** Mods turn Claude Code from a fixed tool into one you shape. The price is the same as for any software you install: trust the source.


## 3


What people built in the first days


The New Stack[reported](https://thenewstack.io/anthropic-claude-code-mods-plugins/) that "Users were already experimenting with more specialized uses within hours of the announcement." Here is what people built, at a glance. Their posts follow.


- **[@kirillvserditov](https://x.com/kirillvserditov/status/2105790255144063241) :** a live progress bar for plans, with stages, sounds and several tasks side by side.
- **[Dom, @dominikmartn](https://x.com/dominikmartn/status/2106044283455406335) :** a mod that shows what a session is working on, and when their mini's disk is about to be full.
- **[Hamza, @thegenioo](https://x.com/thegenioo/status/2106139975922409585) :** a first mod in the Claude Code desktop app.
- **[Sean Nicholas, @sean_snd](https://x.com/sean_snd/status/2105965372956623126) :** a mod that sends encrypted passwords into the chat. Claude can work with them but never reads them.
- **[cc-arcade](https://github.com/sezaakgun/cc-arcade) :** "Tetris, and seven other games, above the prompt, playable while Claude works, zero tokens." Boris Cherny[shared it](https://x.com/bcherny/status/2099551291601248485) before launch.
- **[stepline](https://github.com/saadk408/stepline) :** turns the plan you approve in plan mode into a live checklist above the prompt.
- **[drift](https://github.com/PickleBoxer/drift) :** folder, branch, ahead/behind and uncommitted changes above the prompt.
- **[cc-mod-park](https://github.com/GGGODLIN/cc-mod-park) :** park a session and resume it later from a new session in the same folder.
- **[awesome-claude-code-mods](https://github.com/karanb192/awesome-claude-code-mods) :** a "Community catalogue of public Claude Code mods", to browse more.

## 4


How we used it: a cleaner chat


More and more people ask an AI to do real work on their computer. Claude Code is a tool for exactly that. It is also noisy.


- **Claude shows its work, all of it.** Each file it reads and each command it runs gets its own block on screen.
- **Your own words get buried.** After a few minutes, your question sits far above a wall of commands.
- **The answer is hard to find.** Claude's reply is in there, between results you did not ask to see.


A mod fixes this without changing what Claude does. Claude does the same work. You just see it differently.


So we built one: chat-clean. It keeps your messages and Claude's replies, and folds the work of each turn into one line. It is free and open source. The rest of this guide shows the before and after, how to install it, and how to build your own mod.


**So what?** If you cannot read the chat, you cannot steer the work. A mod gives you back the conversation.


## 5


The words, explained once


This section assumes you know nothing about any of this. If you already use Claude Code, skip tosection 6 .


### The tool


- **Claude.** An AI made by Anthropic. You write to it in plain words and it writes back.
- **Claude Code.** A version of Claude that works on the files of a project. It can read them, change them and run commands.
- **Terminal.** The plain text window where programmers type commands. Claude Code can run there.
- **Desktop app.** The Claude app you install on your computer. It has a Code tab that runs Claude Code in a normal window.
- **Tool call.** One action Claude takes, such as reading a file or running a command. A single request can lead to many.


### The mod


- **Mod.** Short for modification. A small add-on that changes how Claude Code looks. Claude Code calls it a plugin.
- **Plugin.** A folder that Claude Code loads by itself. A mod is one kind of plugin.
- **Hook.** A small piece of code that runs at a set moment. For example, "when Claude finishes a turn" or "when this row is drawn".
- **Row.** One block in the chat: your message, Claude's reply, a tool call, or the band above the input.


### The old way


- **Status line.** One or more lines of text under the input box, in the terminal. Before mods, it was the usual place to add your own information.


**So what?** A mod is not a new AI and not a new feature of Claude. It is a new way to see the same work.


## 6


Before and after


Here is the same small task, run twice. On the left, Claude Code as it comes. On the right, with the chat-clean mod.


**Figure 7.** One request: read some files, run a test, add a small helper, run the test again. Left, Claude Code's own drawing. Right, the same turn with chat-clean: the work folds into`` .


### What changed on screen


- **A name column on the left.**` you` beside your messages,` claude` beside the replies.
- **The time of each of your messages,** at the right edge.
- **One line for the work.** Every tool call of a turn folds into one line:` ○ 7 steps this turn ›` . The arrow opens it in place.
- **A working line while Claude works.** A spinner, the step in plain words, and the time.
- **Plain labels.** A step reads` Reading app.py` or`` . Never a raw command, a path or an id.


### What did not change


- **Claude's work.** The mod changes only the drawing. Claude reads, runs and answers as before.
- **Nothing is lost.** ctrl+o still shows the full transcript.
- **You can switch back any time.** Type` /feed raw` and Claude Code draws everything its own way again.


**So what?** The left side is a log for a machine. The right side is a chat for a person. Both hold the same work.


## 7


Where a clean chat helps


A mod pays off wherever a person needs to follow the work without reading every command.


### Long sessions


- **Many steps per request.** When one request triggers dozens of tool calls, a single line per turn keeps the chat short.
- **Finding your own question again.** Your words stay on screen, with their time.


### Work that keeps running


- **Background runs.** Sometimes a test keeps running after Claude has answered. Then one line above the input says so:` Running in the background · · you can keep typing` .
- **Tests.** A run that looks like a test reads` Test running` .
- **Helpers.** Claude can start helpers, also called subagents. Each gets its own line with its state and time.` /helpers` opens a pane with each helper's steps.


**Figure 8.** Helpers at work, with chat-clean. One summary line counts the helpers that are done and running, then one line per kind of helper shows its progress.


### Moments that need you


- **Errors.** An API error becomes one plain line, for example` ! Connection lost · check your internet · send again to retry` . It is amber when Claude Code handles it, red when you must act.
- **Questions.** When Claude asks you something, the answered question becomes one line:` ? Which colour → Red` .


Before


After, with chat-clean


**Figure 9.** The same lost connection, twice. Claude Code prints the raw error. chat-clean says what happened and what to do.


### People who do not code


- **Managers, analysts, designers.** Anyone who asks Claude for work but does not read shell commands can read a clean chat.


**So what?** The more Claude does on its own, the more you need a calm view of it. That is where a mod earns its place.


## 8


What is better than before


Before mods, the usual way to add your own information to Claude Code was the status line. It still works. A mod goes further.


### How the status line works


- **It is a command.** You name a small program in your settings. Claude Code runs it and prints what it returns, under the input.
- **It can redraw every second.** With`` in the settings, it redraws once a second while you wait.
- **A slow frame shows nothing.** If the program takes longer than the interval, the frame is dropped. Our first version read running jobs with a command that took , and drew nothing at all.
- **The fix was a cache.** A separate background program now does the slow part and saves the result. The status line only reads it, in .

### The same numbers, in more places


- **Usage limits.** A mod can read how much of your you have used. The status line gets the same figures in its input.
- **Memory and cost.** Both can show how full Claude's memory is and what the session has cost.
- **Usage left first.** When we ranked the figures, how much usage was left mattered more than memory.


**So what?** A status line is a sticky note under the window. A mod rearranges the window. Keep the status line for a few figures, and use a mod for the chat itself.


## 9


chat-clean is our open source mod, free under the MIT licence. You need .


### Before you start


- **Claude Code installed.** If you have never used it, install it first from Anthropic's Claude Code page, and open it once in any folder.
- **A project folder.** Any folder you already open with Claude Code. We call it your project.
- **Check your version.** In a terminal, type` claude --version` . The number must be 2.1.289 or higher.


### The three steps


1. **Copy the mod into your project,** as` <project>/.claude/skills/chat-clean/` . The easiest way, from inside your project folder in a terminal:


```text
git clone https://github.com/achammah/claude-chat-clean .claude/skills/chat-clean
```


1. **Start Claude Code in that project.** The mod loads by itself. There is nothing to switch on.
2. **Type` /feed` .** It opens the settings page, so you can see the mod is there.


### Just want to try it


- **No copy needed.** Start Claude Code with` claude --plugin-dir /path/to/chat-clean` . Replace the path with wherever you saved the folder.


### The three views


- **` /feed clean` ,** the default. Your messages, Claude's replies, and one line per turn for the work.
- **` /feed normal` .** Each run of tool calls is one line with counts, for example`` . Nothing is cleared.
- **` /feed raw` .** Claude Code's own drawing. The mod draws nothing.
- **It sticks.** The view you pick is kept for your next sessions.
- **Fine tuning.**` /feed hide <kind>` and` /feed show <kind>` switch one kind of row off or on. The kinds are` you` ,` said` ,` tool` ,` agent` ,` question` ,` peer` ,` helper` and` search` .


**So what?** Three steps, no settings to edit, and one command to undo it all. Try it on your next long task.


## 10


Build your own mod


You do not need to write a mod by hand. You can ask Claude Code to write it for you. It still helps to know the parts, so you can tell when something is wrong.


### Step by step


1. **Ask Claude to load the plugin authoring guide first.** In our version, Claude Code offered a skill called` plugin-authoring` for exactly this. When we skipped it, we drew a whole band as one picture, which is not how mods work.
2. **Make a folder in your project:**` .claude/skills/<your-mod>/` . A plugin folder there loads by itself.
3. **Add a short description:**` .claude-plugin/plugin.json` . It holds the name, version, description and licence.
4. **Point to your code:**` hooks/hooks.json` holds one line,` { "modules": \["./register.tsx"\] }` .
5. **Write the code:**` hooks/register.tsx` . Each hook says when it runs and what it draws. For example, chat-clean's band hook starts with` on('ui.render', { component: 'AbovePrompt' }, ...)` .
6. **Declare what you remember.** If the mod keeps values between moments, name each one in` types/index.d.ts` .
7. **Check it before you look.** Run` claude plugin validate <folder>` , then` claude plugin test <folder>` . Both are fast. Run them after every change.
8. **Save, and watch it reload.** Saving reloads the mod in every open session of that project. In the terminal it is at once.


###


Claude Code refuses a mod that breaks one of these. Each one refused our code at least once.


- **One code file per plugin.**` hooks/hooks.json` names` ./register.tsx` only.
- **One hook per moment.** Two hooks for the same event, in one plugin, do not load.
- **Event names are written out.** A hook name kept in a variable is refused.
- **The engine handle stays in one file.** Pass it only to functions declared in that same file.
- **Every remembered value is declared** in` types/index.d.ts` .
- **No writing while drawing.** Change values from an event, a timer or a button press. A drawing only reads.


### Good habits


- **Batch your saves.** Every save reloads every open session and prints a reload line.
- **Keep motion for when work runs.** There is no animation built in. Motion means redrawing on a timer, such as . Stop the timer at the end of a turn.
- **Use few colours.** One accent, one green, one violet, grey for the rest. Red only when the person must act.


**So what?** A mod is a small folder with one code file. Let Claude write it, and let the two checks tell you if it is right.


## 11


Tweaks for the desktop app


The desktop app runs the same mods, but it is a different screen. Most of our early mistakes were here.


### What is different


- **It runs no status line.** Nothing from the` statusLine` setting appears there. The band above the input is the place for status on desktop.
- **It keeps its own message look.** chat-clean's name column is for the terminal only. On desktop, your messages keep the app's own bubbles.
- **Some rows exist only in the terminal.** The progress, turn duration and info notice rows are terminal only.
- **Reloads wait.** On desktop, a saved mod reloads after` /reload-plugins` or at the end of the next turn.


### What chat-clean shows on desktop


- **One pill with your usage:** how much of you have used.
- **While something runs:** one pill per running helper, background job and test.


###


- **Ask which screen you are on.** Each drawing is told its surface,` terminal` or` desktop` . Branch on it.
- **Keep desktop text short.** The engine counts space in characters, but the desktop draws a wider font. A row of line characters took far more room than counted, and the words after it wrapped.
- **Do not let pills stretch.** A pill that grows can push the next one off the edge. What held: a left group and a right item, nothing stretched, one pill allowed to shrink.
- **Do not lay a box over the words.** A box placed on top draws above what comes after it. Our "fill behind the words" hid the words.
- **Do not draw the band as a picture.** The desktop can draw an image, but an interactive one sits in a . Use images only for a inside a pill.


### Two practical points


- **Permissions.** The desktop starts in the project's permission mode, so it may ask before almost every command. We fixed it with allow rules in the project's settings, not by switching checks off.
- **Look at it.** You cannot see the desktop from a script. A screenshot of the Claude window, then reading it, ended .


**So what?** Build for the screen you will actually use. On desktop, the band above the input replaces the status line, and short beats clever.


## 12


What a mod cannot change


Some rows belong to Claude Code itself. No mod can reach them.


- **Hook rows,** for example or a hook error.
- **The reload line** that appears when a mod reloads.
- **Attachment lines** under a message, for example "Read file" or "Loaded CLAUDE.md".
- **The status line** and the footer's task list.
- **Rows drawn during a reload.** They keep Claude Code's look, because they are already on screen.


**So what?** If you see an old style row in a clean chat, it was almost always drawn during a save. It is not a bug in your mod.
